title: Move Zeroes

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of numbers `nums`.

**Return the list with every zero moved to the end, while every non-zero number keeps its original relative order.**

Do it in a single pass, without allocating a second array to build the answer in.
constraints: nums may contain any mix of positive, negative, and zero values
content.outputFormat: The array with all zeroes moved to the end in-place.
notes: Do it in a single pass without allocating a second array.
Minimize the total number of write operations.

bruteForce.description: Build a new list of the non-zero elements in order, then pad the end with zeroes to the original length.

better.description: Two pointers swapping non-zeroes to front.

optimal.pattern: two pointers: a slow pointer marking where the next non-zero should go, a fast pointer scanning
optimal.description: Slow-pointer overwrite: Walk array with fast pointer, overwrite at slow pointer for every non-zero, then fill remaining slots with zero.

hints: Can you avoid building a whole second array, and instead shift things around as you scan once?
What if a slow pointer marked 'the next spot a non-zero value belongs', and a fast pointer looked for non-zero values to put there?
Walk the array with a fast pointer; every time you find a non-zero value, place it at the slow pointer's position and advance slow.
Once the fast pointer reaches the end, every position from the slow pointer onward should become zero.
followUps: Could you minimize the total number of operations done?
learningObjectives: Minimize write operations when moving elements to array end.
Handle empty arrays and arrays containing only zeroes without edge-case crashes.
